body:
You can do
```suggestion
		return _object_id.is_valid() ? ObjectDB::get_instance<T>(_object_id) : nullptr;
```
btw this was the only part that could cause crash (see #94101), all other validation might be unnecessary.

body:
I might be misunderstanding the old `WeakRef`, but to me, this seems inherently unsafe.

`WeakRef` can be used to longterm store an `ObjectID` (say over a number of frames) without incrementing the ref count (so you can delete it elsewhere).

But when you want to access a refcounted object, you *should* be incrementing the refcount, so it can't be deleted from another thread while you are using it?
